# `Q-2-31` — Inline Code Execution Not Allowed in URLs

> Inline executable code (`` `{lang} expr` ``) cannot appear
> inside the URL portion of a link or image.

## What this means

Quarto supports inline code execution: a backtick run containing
`{language}` followed by an expression evaluates the expression
at render time and inserts the result. This error fires when an
author places that form inside the destination of a link or
image — the `(...)` after `[text]` or `![alt]`.

The URL parser reads the backtick run as part of the URL
literal, so the executable code never runs.

## Why this happens

Most often, an author who wanted to compute a URL dynamically
tried to drop inline execution into the URL slot of a link or
image.

## How to fix

Compute the URL ahead of time in a code chunk, then build the
link or image inside that chunk and emit the result as markdown.
The exact pattern depends on the engine (Python, R, Julia),
but the principle is the same: do not embed inline execution
inside link or image destinations.
